headline: Risk-on tone cools into Wednesday's Fed call and mega-cap earnings
body: Markets carried a genuinely risk-on tone into this week, with stocks closing higher Friday as excitement over Anthropic's IPO filing propelled the tech sector and Wall Street opening the new week on a winning note Monday. That enthusiasm has gone quieter into Tuesday, with futures trading mixed as traders square positions ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision. The setup is unusual for this cycle: the central bank raised rates 25 basis points last month, its first hike since 2023, and while CME FedWatch pricing still puts roughly 90% odds on a hold this week, at least one major bank is dissenting and looking for another increase. Gold easing on a firmer dollar into the announcement reads as a small, genuine hedge against that hawkish tail rather than confident disinflation optimism.

The bigger swing factor may be earnings rather than the Fed itself: roughly 163 S&P 500 companies report this week, with Microsoft and Alphabet due the same afternoon as the rate decision and Amazon a day later. Meta's results last week offer a cautionary marker -- shares fell sharply even on strong headline growth, as investors parsed AI capital spending more skeptically than the top-line beat. That reaction suggests the market's patience with 'spend now, monetize later' framing is thinning even as the broader indices sit near highs. Retail chatter was thin in today's search results, so this read leans more on price action and the week's event calendar than on any observed shift in crowd positioning.
